Name: Nehiyawedew
Author: nehiyawerim
Description:
Nêhiyawêdêw (Cree Stardew Valley) adds 21 Indigenous plants (and 5 new bushes) to Stardew Valley! Each of these additions are Indigenous plants to the prairies (Canada/US) displaying their name in nêhiyawêwin (Cree, Y-dialect), are forage-able according to the time of year you would most likely find or harvest it, and includes a little blurb about the plant or its name!

Please talk to an expert (not me) before harvesting, eating, or otherwise using any of these plants! It would be good to ask someone the appropriate way to harvest them, too, to be respectful of the plant and ensure its continuation.

The following plants are currently added through nêhiyawêdêw:


[list]
[*][b]acimomêyisimin[/b] (a), Prickly Pear (red, orange, and yellow)[/*]
[*][b]âhâsiwimin[/b] (a), Juniper Berry[/*]
[*][b]ayôskan[/b] (ak), Raspberry[/*]
[*][b]cikâsipakwa[/b] (a), Kinnikinnick[/*]
[*][b]mahihkanimin[/b] (a), Wolfberry, Silverberry[/*]
[*][b]maskêkopak[/b] (a), Labrador Tea[/*]
[*][b]misâskwatômin[/b] (a), Saskatoon Berry[/*]
[*][b]mistahiyinimin[/b] (a), Huckleberry[/*]
[*][b]okiniy[/b] (a), Rosehip[/*]
[*][b]pasân[/b] (ak), Cattail[/*]
[*][b]miscanikwacâsôsôs[/b] (a), Horsetail (new shoots and old)[/*]
[*][b]mînisîhkês[/b] (ak), Seneca Root[/*]
[*][b]wâpikwaniy[/b] (a), Wild Rose (also used for flowers, generally)[/*]
[*][b]wîsakipakos[/b] (a), Bitterroot (2x, blooming and not)[/*]
[/list]

After the name of each plant is either an "(a)" or "(ak)", these additions explain how you would refer to multiple of the plant. For example, "mistahiyinimin" means "one huckleberry," and "mistahiyinimina" means "more than one, or many huckleberries."

The -a and -ak also tell you whether the object is considered (at least grammatically) inanimate (-a) or animate (-ak). Huckleberries are inanimate. pasânak (cattails) are animate. 

Nêhiyawêdêw is part of a series of game mods aimed at increasing Indigenous language use, knowledge, and representation of our relations in video games, with the hopes that it will be helpful for those trying to learn (or just want to see more Indigenous content in their games!).

Please note that I am a learner, also, so please reach out if you notice any mistakes and I'll gladly make corrections! Also, I am not an expert in edible or medicinal plants, please consult with experts before harvesting, eating, or otherwise using plants from the wild!

Future updates will include recipes, more complex NPC gift tastes, potentially more plants, and perhaps unique, nêhiyawêwin dialogue options or syllabics (if supported).

I'd like to thank the city of Edmonton for helping support this project through the Funding Indigenous Resurgence Edmonton grant (and for their patience)!

hiy hiy!
